name: Somalia
system_note: A federal system under a provisional constitution, with the president's mandate disputed.
snapshot: Parliament extended the president's term by a year to push through one-person-one-vote elections; the opposition and powerful federal states call his mandate expired.
culture: Somalis are often called a nation of poets: oral poetry has long carried news, politics and love, and a good poet can sway clan elders. Somali is spoken by nearly everyone, giving the country unusual ethnic and linguistic unity despite deep clan divisions. Camel herding, tea and an enormous diaspora in Minneapolis, London and Nairobi tie the culture together.
society: The state collapsed in 1991, and the federal government still controls only parts of the south and centre, fighting al-Shabaab, which runs its own courts and taxes. Somaliland in the north has run itself since 1991 and seeks recognition. Remittances and mobile money keep the economy going, and droughts are frequent and deadly.
situation: Somalia has had no strong central government since the dictator Siad Barre fell in 1991. Since 2004, its leaders have been chosen not by voters but by clan elders who pick MPs who pick the president. Al-Shabaab, al-Qaeda's affiliate, still controls much of the countryside, and a 2025 offensive reversed government gains and put it within reach of Mogadishu (Africa Center for Strategic Studies). In 2026, the fight over how, and whether, to hold elections pushed the country toward another constitutional crisis.

President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud wants Somalia's first one-person, one-vote national elections since 1969. His opponents, including the leaders of the powerful federal states of Puntland and Jubaland, suspect the reform is cover for staying in power. On 4 March, parliament voted by acclamation to extend the terms of MPs and the president from four years to five, pushing elections back a year (Reuters via Polity). The opposition Somali Future Council, which includes two former presidents, declared that parliament's mandate expired on 14 April and the president's on 15 May, and threatened to hold its own parallel election (Dawan Africa). A similar term extension in 2021 split the security forces along clan lines and led to fighting in Mogadishu. Analysts warn of a possible federal military move on Jubaland, while the UAE, Turkey, Egypt and Ethiopia all compete for influence along Somalia's coast. About 11,000 African Union troops remain in the country.
power: A federal parliamentary republic under a provisional constitution. Parliament elects the president, who appoints a prime minister. The federal member states, especially Puntland and Jubaland, act with wide autonomy; Somaliland in the north has operated as a separate, unrecognised state since 1991.
holders: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, re-elected 2022, mandate disputed since May 2026; Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre.
